provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Out family batch. Low-ticket recurring work: every price in the kit is sized for an owner who thinks in weekly mows, and the kit leans on sign-ups, route days and autopay. No mower or software brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Weekly and every-other-week mowing, what's included (mow, edge, trim, blow), prices by lot size band, season length and how to sign up online
pageStructurePlus.why: Lawn customers buy on a clear weekly price. A plan page with sign-up turns a quote call into a subscription.

pageStructurePlus.section: Route days, rain delays and gate access
pageStructurePlus.contains: Which day the crew is on each street, what happens when it rains, gate codes, dogs in the yard, and skipping a week while on holiday
pageStructurePlus.why: Most lawn complaints are about not knowing when the crew comes. Answering it up front keeps customers all season.

pageStructurePlus.section: Spring and fall yard cleanup booking
pageStructurePlus.contains: Leaf removal, bed cleanout, first mow of spring, last mow and leaf mulching in autumn, with booking windows and haul-away options
pageStructurePlus.why: Cleanups are the two biggest tickets in the lawn year and the door to a season of mowing.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Aeration, overseeding, hedge trimming, mulch refresh, weed pulling and gutter leaf clearing, each priced to add to an existing mowing plan
pageStructurePlus.why: Add-ons raise the value of each mowing customer without new stops on the route.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Common-area mowing, entrance beds, seasonal colour, snow tie-ins, monthly service reports and insurance certificates for property managers
pageStructurePlus.why: Contract grounds work evens out the season, and managers look for a lawn company that looks organised.

designDirections.name: Mowed This Week
designDirections.bestFor: Solo and two-person mowing outfits that need one page with prices and a sign-up
designDirections.headlineSample: Weekly lawn mowing in {City}, from your street's route day
designDirections.whyItFits: Citrus warmth feels like a summer Saturday, and the geometric caps make the price and sign-up impossible to miss.

designDirections.name: On the Route
designDirections.bestFor: Lawn companies with several crews selling weekly plans, cleanups and add-ons by route
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's combo. Linen keeps plan cards calm and readable, brick red makes sign-up clear, and slab headings feel local and steady.

designDirections.name: Grounds Contract
designDirections.bestFor: Lawn maintenance firms bidding HOA, office park and church grounds contracts
designDirections.headlineSample: Grounds maintenance for {City} HOAs and properties
designDirections.whyItFits: Evergreen and an old-style serif read like a facilities proposal, which is how managers compare lawn contractors.

openers.line: Someone new to {City} searching for lawn mowing finds {Business Name} with a phone number and no site. They want to see a weekly price and whether you cover their street.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a new mowing customer would see: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing goes to Facebook, where 'taking new lawn customers' is a post from back in spring. Someone moving in wants a mowing price and a sign-up, not a scroll.
openers.hook: Tap the link and confirm it goes to Facebook. Note any 'taking new customers' post.
openers.linkLine: A lawn care page with prices and sign-up: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site still lists last season's mowing prices on a free host. Lawn customers sign up in spring, and an old price list makes them call someone else.
openers.hook: Open their site and look for an old year, old prices or a builder banner. Note which.

openers.line: On a phone your lawn site's price table runs off the screen. Most people looking for a mowing service are on their phone looking at their own grass.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your lawn prices, readable on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to sign up for weekly mowing with {Business Name} without a call and a back-and-forth. A sign-up with lot size and gate code would fill your route while you mow.
openers.hook: Check listing, bios and any site for a sign-up or booking. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A mowing sign-up with lot size, gate code and route day: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your striped lawns and crisp edges on Instagram are what people want their yard to look like. There's no page that turns that into a weekly lawn care sign-up.
openers.hook: Find two clean striped lawns or edges they posted. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your best lawns next to a sign-up button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say the crew shows up the same day every week and never misses a gate. That's what lawn customers care about most, and it stays on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about reliability. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to your mowing plans: {demo-link}

openers.line: Lawn customers pick their mowing company in March and stick with it all year. The outfit with a sign-up page in March fills its routes first.
openers.hook: Use from February to April, or late summer for fall cleanups. Name the month.

openers.line: People decide to hire a lawn service on Sunday evening after mowing it themselves one more time. A sign-up that works then gets them on Tuesday's route.
openers.hook: Message or call on a weekend evening. If nothing comes back until Monday, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A mowing sign-up that works on Sunday night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring for the lawn crew. Reliable workers pick the company that looks organised, the same way customers do.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A lawn company site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your mowing route covers a few neighbourhoods, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you're already on their street. That's the easiest sale in lawn care.
openers.hook: Find neighbourhoods named in reviews or posts; use one where they clearly have customers.
openers.linkLine: A lawn page for each neighbourhood on the route: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer a discount for prepaying the mowing season or autopay, put it on the sign-up. Lawn customers like a simple monthly number.
openers.hook: Only if they mention prepay or autopay anywhere. Otherwise skip.
openers.linkLine: Prepaid lawn seasons and autopay explained: {demo-link}

openers.line: A mower throws a rock through a window now and then. Showing your insurance on a page tells careful lawn customers you're the real thing, not a kid with a trailer.
openers.hook: Look for any mention of insurance. Note what's there; never invent terms.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and service promise on one lawn page: {demo-link}

openers.line: When one house on a street gets mowed weekly, the neighbours notice the stripes. They still look you up before calling.
openers.hook: Look for reviews mentioning neighbours. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next lawn referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a sharp-looking lawn, clean edges and even stripes. That's the yard that should sell your mowing plan.
openers.hook: Pick their newest lawn or cleanup post and name it: stripes, edging, cleanup, town if tagged.

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted has some of the cleanest stripes I've seen.

I was looking for lawn mowing services in {City} and found {Business Name} on Maps, but no site where someone can see your weekly price and sign up for your route. I put together a sample lawn care site, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample lawn care site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has mowing plans by lot size, an online sign-up with gate code and route day, and cleanup booking for spring and fall. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave it.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build simple websites for lawn care companies in {City}. I sent you a message about a sample site. Did you see it?"

IF NO:
"No problem. It's a small lawn site for {Business Name}: mowing prices by lot size, an online sign-up and cleanup booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, then ask how many new mowing customers they want this season
"It's {Build Range}, kept small on purpose, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For your outfit I'd quote about {Build Price}. A handful of new weekly lawns covers it."
"Ten minutes this week to look at it?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and a deposit invoice. It's live before spring sign-ups."

objections.handler: "Then the site helps you pick tighter routes. Sign-ups from your own streets mean less drive time, and you can turn off the form when you're full."

objections.objection: Lawn work doesn't pay enough for a website.
objections.handler: "That's why this one is small and priced for mowing. A handful of new weekly lawns pays for it in the first season."
"Nextdoor is great for the first mention. People still click through to see your prices and sign up. Right now there's nowhere to click."

objections.objection: My kid can make me a site.
objections.handler: "Go for it. If you want, I'll hand over the plan table and the sign-up layout. If it stalls before spring, call me."

objections.objection: I don't want to post prices.
objections.handler: "We can show a starting price by lot size and confirm after a look. Mowing customers want a ballpark before they call anyone."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: mowing plans, sign-up, cleanup booking and a page for each neighbourhood on the route."

email.subject: Lawn care site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build small websites for lawn care companies in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name}. I'll text the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} lawn demo down on Friday.

Keep it up for you? A quick yes or no works.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, spring mowing sign-ups are about to start. Thought of {Business Name}.

The small lawn site is still up, same price: {demo-link}

bullets: Keep the build small. A mowing company should earn it back from a handful of new weekly lawns in one season.
The online sign-up with lot size, gate code and route day is the whole point; never cut it to save money.
Price neighbourhood pages cheaply; they match how mowing routes are actually built.
Sell monthly products in tens of dollars, not hundreds; this owner prices in weekly mows.
Add the commercial grounds page only for outfits that want HOA or office contracts.
Skip galleries beyond a few strong lawns; lawn customers buy reliability and price, not a portfolio.

lineItems.item: Online mowing sign-up with route day
lineItems.description: Max with lot-size pricing, gate code, pet notes, start date and autopay sign-up.

lineItems.item: Cleanup booking for spring and fall
lineItems.description: Max with picture upload of the yard, haul-away options and booking windows.
Max when each add-on can be ticked onto an existing mowing plan online.
Max when each page shows the route day and a lawn from that neighbourhood.
Max with sample service reports, insurance details and a bid request form.
Max when the sign-up, plans and route-day page are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the lawn route
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A striped lawn or a finished cleanup goes on your Maps profile each week with the neighbourhood, and your hours stay right through winter."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after the first mow
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After a new customer's first mow, they get a text asking for a review. With weekly lawns, reviews add up fast."

whatElseYouSell.name: Route-street door hangers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Door hangers on the houses next to your lawns on each route day: 'We already mow your street on Tuesdays.' That's the cheapest mowing customer you'll ever get."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, on each route day with room to grow.

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring sign-up push
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short campaign in late winter for weekly mowing plans fills your routes before the grass grows."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in January, run February to March.

whatElseYouSell.name: Trailer and truck door artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your trailer is parked on a lawn customer's street every week. Put the sign-up site on it and the neighbours read it all season."

whatElseYouSell.name: Fall cleanup and aeration campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "An autumn offer to existing mowing customers for leaf cleanup and aeration adds a ticket to every lawn you already service."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in August, run September to October.

whatElseYouSell.name: Nextdoor recommendation prompt cards
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A small card left after the first mow asks happy lawn customers to recommend you on Nextdoor, with the site address."

withoutAI.route: Irrigation techs who fix the sprinklers you mow over
withoutAI.whoPays: The irrigation company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your mowing crews spot broken sprinkler heads every week. The irrigation tech you call needs a site, and he'll send lawn customers back."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Mowers see the problem; irrigation fixes it. A natural two-way referral.

withoutAI.whoPays: The lawn treatment company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The fertiliser and weed control company on the same lawns doesn't mow. Their site can send mowing to you, yours sends treatments to them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Treatment and mowing are separate trades on the same lawn.

withoutAI.whoPays: The mower dealer and repair shop
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The shop that sharpens your blades has every lawn crew in town as a customer. A service booking site helps them, and you make the intro."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Dealers have budgets and a customer list of lawn businesses.

withoutAI.whoPays: The snow removal contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "If you don't plow, the outfit that does can take your lawn customers in winter and send them back in spring. They need a site too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Seasonal trades hand customers back and forth.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Agents need empty listings mowed and managers need rentals kept up. A vendor request page puts your lawn crew on their list."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Steady, simple work from people who refer constantly.

withoutAI.whoPays: The gutter cleaning company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The gutter cleaner works the same streets in autumn as your leaf cleanups. Trade referrals and both of you fill the season."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same customer, same season, different ladder.

withAI.route: Treatment upsell spotter for the weed control company
withAI.pitchLine: "Your partner treats lawns but never sees them weekly. The mowing crew flags thin, weedy turf from the route and the treatment company gets a ready-made lead."
withAI.whyItWorks: The treatment company gets warm leads; the lawn crew earns goodwill or a fee.

withAI.route: Repair booking assistant for the mower shop
withAI.pitchLine: "Lawn crews text a picture of the broken mower and the assistant books a repair slot and says what parts to expect."
withAI.whyItWorks: Spring repair rushes swamp the counter; crews want faster turnarounds.

withAI.route: Vacant listing yard check for realtors
withAI.pitchLine: "After each mow, the agent gets a picture and a short note confirming the listing's lawn is ready for showings."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents need proof without driving out; the lawn crew becomes their default.

withAI.route: Winter handoff messages for the snow contractor
withAI.pitchLine: "In late autumn, lawn customers get a message introducing the snow partner, and in spring the mowing restart offer goes out."
withAI.whyItWorks: Both seasonal businesses keep customers year-round.

withAI.route: Resident request sorter for HOA grounds
withAI.pitchLine: "Residents report missed mowing or overgrown common areas with a picture; the assistant groups them into one weekly lawn work order."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers stop forwarding single emails; the lawn client gets clear tickets.

withAI.route: Gutter and leaf cleanup bundle assistant
withAI.pitchLine: "Autumn customers asking for gutter cleaning get offered a leaf cleanup bundle with your lawn crew, booked in one exchange."
withAI.whyItWorks: Bundled autumn work for both trades from one enquiry.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for mowing enquiries
softwareAI.pitchLine: "You can't hear the phone over the mower. The caller gets a text with your mowing sign-up link and a question about their lot size."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Autopay for weekly lawn plans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Mowing customers are charged monthly on the card on file, with a receipt listing each mow. No more chasing cheques under doormats."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 1. Needs their payment account and plan prices.

softwareAI.name: Lot-size price lookup by address
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner types their address, picks a lot size band and sees the weekly mowing price straight away."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their price bands and service area.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for lawn customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each review gets a reply drafted that mentions the lawn and the crew, ready to approve on a break."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Rain delay texts by route
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When rain pushes Tuesday's mowing route to Wednesday, every customer on it gets a text. The 'where's my crew' calls stop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their routes listed by day.

softwareAI.name: Route builder for new sign-ups
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New lawn sign-ups drop onto the right route day by street, so each crew's day stays tight and drive time stays low."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their current routes and crew capacity.

softwareAI.name: Lawn chatbot on plans, schedules and add-ons
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'what day do you mow my street' and 'do you bag clippings' from your own answers, and signs people up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their plan details and route days. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Skip-a-week and pause requests
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers going on holiday pause their mowing online, and the crew's route sheet updates automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the route builder in place.

softwareAI.name: Yard picture cleanup quote
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers upload pictures of an overgrown yard or a leaf-covered lawn, and the tool drafts a cleanup price range for you to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a set of past cleanups with pictures and prices. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Crew route sheet on the phone
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each crew sees today's lawns in order, gate codes, dog notes and add-ons, and taps each one done."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs routes and customer notes.

softwareAI.name: Season renewal and price update messages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before spring, every lawn customer gets a renewal with this year's mowing price and one tap to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, before the next season. Needs the customer list and new prices.

softwareAI.name: Missed-spot complaint triage
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers send a picture of a missed strip or clippings on the drive; the assistant logs it for the crew and replies with when it'll be fixed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their fix-it policy. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Add-on upsell at sign-up
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When someone signs up for mowing, the form offers hedge trimming, aeration and mulch at a plan-holder price."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their add-on prices.

softwareAI.name: Voice notes to lawn estimate
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the yard, say lot size, slopes, beds and gates into the phone, and it drafts the mowing estimate."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Weekly route summary for the owner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every Friday it drafts a short note: lawns mowed, skips, complaints, new sign-ups and which route has room."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the route sheet in use. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with mow history
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers see their mowing dates, invoices and add-ons, and update the card or gate code themselves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs autopay and the route sheet in place.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per lawn
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which lawns actually pay once drive time and minutes on site are counted, so you reprice the ones losing money."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs a season of route times.

softwareAI.name: HOA grounds service report generator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After each visit, the HOA gets a lawn and grounds report with pictures, work done and requests answered."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, once they hold an HOA contract. Needs their checklist.

softwareAI.name: Neighbour referral reward texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Happy mowing customers get a personalised text offering a free mow for each neighbour they refer, written in your voice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their referral offer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for lawn crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Spring hiring means a pile of texts from people who have never pushed a mower. A short chat weeds them out and books interviews with the crew-ready ones."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they hire. Needs must-haves and pay. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Mowing sign-up and route kit for solo operators
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every one-trailer mowing outfit needs the same sign-up, route day and autopay. Priced in tens of dollars a month, it sells to all of them."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Low price, a large pool of operators, identical workflow.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Equipment dealer's lawn business starter page
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Everyone who buys a commercial mower from you is starting a lawn business. Give them a starter site as part of the purchase."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Dealers want to sell more commercial mowers and keep customers loyal.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members switch on a mowing plan page, sign-up and route-day booking as a membership perk."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Small lawn firms are the bulk of members and the least online.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Agencies can't make money on lawn clients at full build prices. A ready mowing template lets them serve the low end profitably."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: It turns unprofitable small clients into profitable ones for agencies.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The lawn care franchise, per territory
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each lawn franchise owner gets local sign-up, their own route days and neighbourhood pages, instead of one corporate form."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Territory owners pay for local sign-ups that fill their routes.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: HOA grounds portal for management firms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every community you manage gets one place for grounds requests, mowing schedules and service reports from its lawn contractor."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Firms with many communities buy once; grounds complaints are constant.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Senior mowing program for councils on aging
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The local council on aging or nonprofit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Seniors request help mowing, volunteers or vetted lawn crews pick up the jobs, and the nonprofit tracks it in one place."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Nonprofits get grants for home help and need a simple system.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Vacant property lawn service for banks and investors
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Vacant homes need mowing with picture proof every visit. A work order and photo log site wins those contracts for local lawn crews."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Preservation companies need proof and reliability; the lawn client provides both.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly note on mowing prices by lot size in the region, built only from rates lawn operators share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Small operators underprice constantly; shared data helps them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Student lawn business starter for trade programs
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The vocational school or youth program
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Students starting a mowing business learn sign-ups, routes and invoicing on a real lawn care site template."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Programs need practical tools; the template is already built.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A lawn company in another suburb
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Mowing is won street by street. I build for one lawn outfit per suburb, and yours doesn't have one yet."

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue lawn sites with no sign-up
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The lawn company with a dead-end site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "If your lawn site is a phone number and a stock picture, I can add sign-up, route days and autopay in a week."

upsellLadder.offer: Lawn site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The lawn site and the care plan go on one contract, so changing mowing prices in spring is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first online sign-up comes in, or they mention chasing a late payment.
upsellLadder.line: "Your first online mowing sign-up is in. Let's put their card on autopay before the first mow."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks and Google profile upkeep
upsellLadder.trigger: A month of weekly mows done for new customers from the site.
upsellLadder.line: "Your new lawn customers have had four mows each. That's the time to ask for reviews."

upsellLadder.trigger: A rainy week brings 'where's my crew' calls.
upsellLadder.line: "Those calls in the rain week are what this stops. One text per mowing route."

upsellLadder.trigger: Sign-ups start landing on streets off their current routes.
upsellLadder.line: "New lawns are coming in from all over. The route builder slots them onto the right mowing day."

upsellLadder.trigger: Late summer arrives with a full list of mowing customers.
upsellLadder.line: "Every lawn you mow needs a leaf cleanup. One offer to your list fills October."

upsellLadder.offer: Season renewal and price update messages
upsellLadder.trigger: Winter, with next season's prices decided.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's renew every lawn customer at this year's price before anyone else knocks on their door."
